title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
重要本节考纲要求



考生需要能够：

对不超过 \(3\times3\) 的矩阵进行加、减、乘运算，并识别零矩阵与单位矩阵；
判断方阵是 singular 还是 non-singular，计算 \(2\times2\)、\(3\times3\) 行列式和非奇异矩阵的逆；
使用 \((AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}\)，并推广到多个矩阵的乘积；
用 \(2\times2\) 矩阵表示旋转、反射、放大、伸缩、剪切等平面变换；
理解复合变换的顺序：\(AB\) 表示先作 \(B\)，再作 \(A\)；
使用 \(|\det M|\) 求面积伸缩因子；
求矩阵变换下的不动点与不变直线。

title: 1.4 Matrices
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Matrix operations
只有阶数相同的矩阵可以相加或相减。若 \(A\) 为 \(m\times n\)，\(B\) 为 \(n\times p\)，则 \(AB\) 有定义且为 \(m\times p\)。
矩阵乘法一般不满足交换律：
\[
AB\ne BA,
\]
但满足结合律与分配律。单位矩阵 \(I\) 满足 \(AI=IA=A\)，零矩阵记作 \(O\)。


1.2 Determinants and inverses
对于
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
\det A=ad-bc.
\]
若 \(\det A=0\)，则 \(A\) singular，不存在逆矩阵；若 \(\det A\ne0\)，则
\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
对 \(3\times3\) 矩阵可按任意一行或一列展开行列式；逆矩阵可由余子式、代数余子式和伴随矩阵求得：
\[
A^{-1}=\frac1{\det A}\operatorname{adj}A.
\]


1.3 Products and inverse order
若 \(A,B\) 均非奇异，
\[
(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}.
\]
右侧顺序必须反转。对三个矩阵，
\[
(ABC)^{-1}=C^{-1}B^{-1}A^{-1}.
\]


1.4 Matrices as transformations
若
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix},
\]
则
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x'\\y'\end{pmatrix}
=M\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
矩阵第一列是 \(\binom10\) 的像，第二列是 \(\binom01\) 的像。常用矩阵包括
\[
R_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},
\]
以及
\[
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&k\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1&h\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\k&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


1.5 Successive transformations and area
若先作 \(B\)、再作 \(A\)，复合矩阵为 \(AB\)。矩阵 \(M\) 所表示变换的面积伸缩因子为
\[
|\det M|.
\]
行列式的符号还反映方向是否翻转。


1.6 Invariant points and lines
不动点 \(\mathbf{x}\) 满足
\[
M\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{x},
\]
即 \((M-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf0\)。
若过原点的直线 \(y=mx\) 在变换后仍映到自身，则方向向量 \(\binom1m\) 的像必须仍与 \(\binom1m\) 平行。对于一般直线 \(y=mx+c\)，应把像点代回同一条直线并比较系数。

2. Textbook Examples

Example 1.1 · Page 8
Find
\[
\begin{pmatrix}10&3\\-2&7\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}5\\2\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Taking each row against the column gives
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}56\\4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.2 · Page 9
Find
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\-2&5\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}4&3&0\\-2&-3&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

The product has order \(2\times3\):
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}-2&-6&3\\-18&-21&5\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.3 · Page 9
Multiply
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\-1&4\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
and state what you notice.


Show solution

\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\-1&4\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Multiplication by the identity matrix has no effect.

 Completed


Example 1.4 · Page 16
Describe the transformations represented by
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

The first matrix interchanges the coordinates, so it is reflection in \(y=x\). The second multiplies both coordinates by \(2\), so it is an enlargement of scale factor \(2\) about the origin.

 Completed


Example 1.5 · Pages 16–18
Find the matrices representing:

reflection in the \(x\)-axis;
enlargement of scale factor \(3\) about the origin.



Show solution

Use the images of \(\binom10\) and \(\binom01\) as the columns:
\[
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}},
\qquad
\boxed{\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]


      xy O    ST(S) reflection in x-axis, then enlargement ×3


Example 1.5: the reflected image lies below the x-axis and every distance from the origin is tripled.



 Completed


Example 1.6 · Pages 19–20
(i) Find the matrix for anticlockwise rotation through \(\theta\) about the origin.
(ii) Hence give the matrix for an anticlockwise rotation through \(60^\circ\).


Show solution

\[
\boxed{R_\theta=
\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{R_{60^\circ}=
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.7 · Pages 21–22
The rectangle has vertices \(A(-1,2)\), \(B(1,2)\), \(C(1,-1)\) and \(D(-1,-1)\). Find its image under
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Multiplying the coordinate matrix gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&1&-1\\2&2&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}5&7&-2&-4\\2&2&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{A'(5,2),\ B'(7,2),\ C'(-2,-1),\ D'(-4,-1)}.
\]


      xy O   originalimage   x-axis fixed; horizontal displacement is proportional to y


Example 1.7: a shear preserves height and area while slanting the vertical sides.



 Completed


Example 1.8 · Pages 23–24
In a shear \(S\), the \(y\)-axis is fixed and \((1,0)\) maps to \((1,5)\). Find the matrix of \(S\).


Show solution

The images of the basis vectors are \(\binom15\) and \(\binom01\), so
\[
\boxed{S=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\5&1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.9 · Pages 29–30
Let \(A,B,C\) represent anticlockwise rotations through \(135^\circ\), \(45^\circ\), \(90^\circ\), respectively.

Write down the matrices.
Verify \(A=BC\).
Calculate \(B^3\) and comment.



Show solution

Using \(R_\theta\) gives the three matrices. Since successive anticlockwise rotations add their angles,
\[
\boxed{BC=R_{45^\circ}R_{90^\circ}=R_{135^\circ}=A},
\]
and similarly
\[
\boxed{B^3=R_{135^\circ}=A}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.10 · Page 33
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(i) Show that \((5,5)\) is invariant. (ii) Find all invariant points.


Show solution

Direct multiplication maps \(\binom55\) to itself. In general,
\[
M\binom{x}{y}=\binom{x}{y}
\]
gives \(2x-y=x\) and \(x=y\). Hence every invariant point lies on
\[
\boxed{y=x}.
\]

 Completed


Example 1.11 · Pages 34–35
Find the invariant lines of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}5&1\\2&4\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Put \(y=mx+c\) and require the image point to satisfy the same equation. Comparing coefficients gives
\[
m^2+m-2=0,
\qquad
(m-3)c=0.
\]
Therefore \(c=0\) and
\[
\boxed{y=x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-2x}.
\]


      xy O    y = x y = −2x points may move, but each whole line maps onto itself


Example 1.11: an invariant line need not be a line of invariant points.



 Completed


Example 6.1 · Page 137
A shape of area \(8\text{ cm}^2\) is transformed by
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\3&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Find the image area.


Show solution

\(\det M=6\), so the area scale factor is \(6\). The image area is
\[
\boxed{48\text{ cm}^2}.
\]

 Completed


Example 6.2 · Pages 137–138
The unit square is transformed by
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\4&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Find its image vertices, \(\det M\), and the image area.


Show solution

The four vertices map to \((0,0),(2,4),(5,5),(3,1)\). Also
\[
\det M=2-12=-10.
\]
Hence the image area is \(\boxed{10}\) square units.


      xy O   SM(S) area image = |det M| × area original


Example 6.2: the determinant gives the signed area factor; its absolute value gives the area scale factor.



 Completed


Example 6.3 · Page 138
Given
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Q=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\]
find \(\det P\), \(\det Q\), and \(\det(PQ)\).


Show solution

\[
\det P=2,\qquad \det Q=3,
\]
and
\[
PQ=\begin{pmatrix}5&4\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det(PQ)=6.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{\det(PQ)=\det P\det Q}\).

 Completed


Example 6.4 · Page 142
Write down matrices \(A,B\) for rotations through \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise and clockwise, and find \(AB\).


Show solution

\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{AB=I},
\]
so the two matrices represent inverse transformations.

 Completed


Example 6.5 · Page 144
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}11&3\\6&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(i) Find \(A^{-1}\). (ii) If \(A\) maps \(P\) to \(Q(5,2)\), find \(P\).


Show solution

Since \(\det A=4\),
\[
\boxed{A^{-1}=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}2&-3\\-6&11\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Then
\[
A^{-1}\binom52=\binom1{-2},
\]
so \(\boxed{P=(1,-2)}\).

 Completed


Example 6.6 · Page 148
Find the determinant of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-4\\7&2&-1\\-2&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]


Show solution

Expanding along the top row,
\[
\det M
=3\begin{vmatrix}2&-1\\1&3\end{vmatrix}
-4\begin{vmatrix}7&2\\-2&1\end{vmatrix}
=21-44.
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{\det M=-23}\).

 Completed


Example 6.7 · Pages 150–151
Find the inverse of
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}2&3&4\\2&-5&2\\-3&6&-3\end{pmatrix}
\]
without a calculator.


Show solution

The determinant is \(-6\). The cofactor matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-3\\33&6&-21\\26&4&-16\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Transpose and divide by \(-6\):
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac16
\begin{pmatrix}-3&-33&-26\\0&-6&-4\\3&21&16\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
Multiplication verifies \(MM^{-1}=I\).

 Completed

4. Past-paper question bank






注记



2019 Paper 1 中检出的矩阵题属于旧考纲的 eigenvalues、diagonalisation 或四维变换，因此不收入本节。以下题目按完全相同的地区版本合并，答案依据对应的 Cambridge mark scheme 整理。



2020



2020 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 6 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) The transformation represented by \(A^{-1}\) maps a triangle of area \(30\text{ cm}^2\) to a triangle of area \(d\text{ cm}^2\). Find \(d\). [3]
(b) Prove by induction that, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[5]
Let \(B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\33&0\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) The line \(y=2x\) is invariant under the transformation represented by \(A^nB\). Find \(n\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since
\[
\det A=2,\qquad \det(A^{-1})=(\det A)^{-1}=\frac12,
\]
the area scale factor is \(\left|\det(A^{-1})\right|=\frac12\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{d=30\times\frac12=15}.
\]
(b) For \(n=1\),
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^1&0\\2^1-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the statement is true initially. Assume that it is true for \(n=k\), where \(k\) is a positive integer:
\[
A^k=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
A^{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}2^k&0\\2^k-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2^{k+1}&0\\2^{k+1}-1&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
Thus the statement is true for \(k+1\) whenever it is true for \(k\). Hence, by mathematical induction,
\[
\boxed{A^n=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n-1&1\end{pmatrix}}
\]
for every positive integer \(n\).
(c) Using part (b),
\[
A^nB=\begin{pmatrix}2^n&0\\2^n+32&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a general point \((x,y)\),
\[
A^nB\binom xy
=\binom{2^nx}{(2^n+32)x}.
\]
The image has gradient \((2^n+32)/2^n\). Since the invariant line has gradient \(2\),
\[
\frac{2^n+32}{2^n}=2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2^n=32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{n=5}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2020, Q6; 9231/12/M/J/2020, Q6.





2020 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 4 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}k&0&2\\0&-1&-1\\1&1&-k\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3\\-1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}-3&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Show that \(A\) is non-singular. [3]
It is given that
\[
CAB=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Find \(k\). [3]
(c) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(CAB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Expanding along the first row,
\[
\det A
=k\begin{vmatrix}-1&-1\\1&-k\end{vmatrix}
+2\begin{vmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{vmatrix}
=k(k+1)+2
=k^2+k+2.
\]
The discriminant of \(k^2+k+2\) is
\[
1^2-4(1)(2)=-7<0.
\]
Since its leading coefficient is positive, \(k^2+k+2>0\) for every real \(k\). Thus \(\det A\ne0\) and \(A\) is non-singular.
(b) First,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}0&-3k\\1&-3\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
and hence
\[
CAB
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&9k+3\\-1&-3k-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Comparing, for example, the top-right entry with the given matrix,
\[
9k+3=-\frac32
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{k=-\frac12}.
\]
(c) The given \(CAB\) maps a point \((x,y)\) to
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}-2&-\frac32\\-1&-\frac32\end{pmatrix}
\binom xy
=\binom{-2x-\frac32y}{-x-\frac32y}.
\]
For the line \(y=mx\), substitute \(y=mx\) and require \(Y=mX\):
\[
-1-\frac32m=m\left(-2-\frac32m\right),
\]
Thus
\[
3m^2+m-2=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(3m-2)(m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=\frac23x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2020, Q4.





2020 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 1 · 9 marks
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(a,b>0\).
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
The unit square is mapped by \(M\) onto parallelogram \(OPQR\).
(b) Find the matrix mapping \(OPQR\) back onto the unit square. [2]
(c) Given that the area of \(OPQR\) is \(2\text{ cm}^2\) and \(x+3y=0\) is invariant, find \(a\) and \(b\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first apply a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(a\), then a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed, taking \((0,1)\) to \((b,1)\).
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Since \(\det M=a\),
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac1a\begin{pmatrix}1&-b\\0&a\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(c) The unit square has area \(1\), so its image has area
\[
|\det M|=a.
\]
As \(a>0\) and the given area is \(2\), \(\boxed{a=2}\). A general point on \(x+3y=0\) can be written as \((x,-x/3)\). Its image is
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{-x/3}
=\binom{ax-\frac13bx}{-\frac13x}.
\]
The image must again satisfy \(X+3Y=0\):
\[
ax-\frac13bx-x=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
1=a-\frac b3.
\]
Using \(a=2\) gives \(\boxed{b=3}\), so \(\boxed{a=2, b=3}\).

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2020, Q1; 9231/13/O/N/2020, Q1.





2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 13 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Identify the transformation represented by \(A\). [1]
(b) Identify the transformation represented by \(B\). [2]
Triangle \(DEF\) is transformed by \(AB\) onto triangle \(PQR\).
(c) Show that the two triangles have the same area. [3]
(d) Find the matrix mapping \(PQR\) onto \(DEF\). [2]
(e) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(AB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) represents reflection in the line \(y=x\).
(b) Comparing \(B\) with the standard rotation matrix shows that it represents a rotation through \(60^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin.
(c) Multiplying in the stated order,
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det(AB)=-1,
\]
Therefore the area scale factor is \(|\det(AB)|=1\), so triangles \(DEF\) and \(PQR\) have equal area.
(d) Using the \(2\times2\) inverse formula,
\[
\boxed{(AB)^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\\[2pt]\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(e) Under \(AB\),
\[
\binom XY
=\binom{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}x+\frac12y}{\frac12x-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}y}.
\]
Put \(y=mx\) and require \(Y=mX\):
\[
\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}m
=m\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac12m\right).
\]
Hence
\[
m^2+2\sqrt3m-1=0,
\]
so \(m=-\sqrt3\pm2\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=(2-\sqrt3)x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-(2+\sqrt3)x}.
\]


      xy O    y = (2 − √3)x y = −(2 + √3)x


2020 O/N 12 Q4: the two invariant directions are perpendicular, as expected for a reflection.



 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2020, Q4.




2021



2021 May/June · 9231/11 & 9231/12 · Question 4 · 14 marks
A rotation of \(60^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin is followed by a one-way stretch in the \(x\)-direction with scale factor \(d\), where \(d\ne0\).
(a) Find the matrix \(M\) of the combined transformation. [4]
(b) The unit square is mapped by \(M\) onto a parallelogram of area \(\frac12d^2\). Show that \(d=2\). [2]
Let \(N\) satisfy
\[
MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(c) Find \(N\). [3]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(MN\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The rotation matrix is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the following stretch has matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}d&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\). Hence, in the correct order,
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}d&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}\frac d2&-\frac{d\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Since
\[
\det M=\frac d4+\frac{3d}{4}=d,
\]
the image area is \(|d|\). In the geometrical stretch context \(d>0\), so
\[
d=\frac12d^2.
\]
As \(d\ne0\), \(\boxed{d=2}\).
(c) With \(d=2\),
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\sqrt3\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\sqrt3\\[2pt]-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
N=M^{-1}(MN)
=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\sqrt3\\[2pt]-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{N=\frac14\begin{pmatrix}1+\sqrt3&1+\sqrt3\\1-\sqrt3&1-\sqrt3\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Under \(MN\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\[2pt]\frac12&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\binom xy

\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},
\qquad 0<\theta<2\pi.
\]
(a) State the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [2]
(b) Find the value of \(\theta\) for which the transformation has a line of invariant points. [7]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Reading the product from right to left, first rotate anticlockwise through \(\theta\) about the origin, then apply a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed and \((0,1)\) mapped to \((2,1)\).
(b) Multiplying gives
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta+2\sin\theta&2\cos\theta-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a line of invariant points there must be a non-zero solution of
\[
M\binom xy=\binom xy.
\]
Equating coordinates gives
\[
(\cos\theta+2\sin\theta-1)x
+(2\cos\theta-\sin\theta)y=0,
\]
\[
\sin\theta\,x+(\cos\theta-1)y=0.
\]
These homogeneous equations have a non-zero solution only when the determinant of their coefficient matrix is zero:
\[
(\cos\theta+2\sin\theta-1)(\cos\theta-1)
-(2\cos\theta-\sin\theta)\sin\theta=0.
\]
Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) simplifies this to
\[
\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\sqrt2\sin\left(\theta+\frac\pi4\right)=1.
\]
In \(0<\theta<2\pi\), the solutions of \(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=1\) are \(\theta=\pi/2\) and the excluded endpoint \(\theta=0\) (equivalently \(2\pi\)). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\theta=\frac\pi2}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/M/J/2025, Q4; 9231/12/M/J/2025, Q4.





2025 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 1 · 11 marks
A one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(14\) is followed by a rotation anticlockwise about the origin through \(\pi/3\). Let the combined matrix be \(M\).
(a) Show that
\[
2M=\begin{pmatrix}14&-\sqrt3\\14\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
[4]
(b) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(M\). [5]
(c) Find \(M^{-1}\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The stretch and rotation matrices are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since the stretch is performed first,
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]\frac{\sqrt3}{2}&\frac12\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}14&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}7&-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]7\sqrt3&\frac12\end{pmatrix},
\]
and multiplying by \(2\) proves the stated result.
(b) For a point \((x,mx)\),
\[
X=7x-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}mx,
\qquad
Y=7\sqrt3x+\frac12mx.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
\sqrt3m^2-13m+14\sqrt3=0.
\]
The discriminant is \(169-168=1\), so
\[
m=\frac{13\pm1}{2\sqrt3}
=2\sqrt3\quad\text{or}\quad\frac7{\sqrt3}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{y=2\sqrt3x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac7{\sqrt3}x}.
\]
(c) Since \(\det M=14\),
\[
M^{-1}
=\frac1{14}\begin{pmatrix}\frac12&\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\[2pt]-7\sqrt3&7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1/14&\sqrt3/14\\-\sqrt3&1\end{pmatrix}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/13/M/J/2025, Q1.





2025 May/June · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks
A one-way stretch in the \(x\)-direction with scale factor \(3\) is followed by reflection in \(y=x\).
(a) Find the combined matrix \(M\). [3]
(b) Give full details of the transformation represented by \(M^{-1}\). [3]
Let \(N\) satisfy \(MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}\).
(c) Find \(N\). [3]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(MN\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) The stretch and reflection matrices are
\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The stretch is followed by the reflection, so
\[
\boxed{M=FS
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\3&0\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(b)
\[
M^{-1}=S^{-1}F^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}1/3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/3\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus \(M^{-1}\) represents reflection in \(y=x\), followed by a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(1/3\).
(c) Since \(MN=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}\),
\[
N=M^{-1}(MN)
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/3\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{N=M^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2/3\\1&2\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) For \(y=mx\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&2\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{mx}
=\binom{(1+2m)x}{(3+2m)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
3+2m=m(1+2m)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2m^2-m-3=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(2m-3)(m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=\frac32x\quad\text{or}\quad y=-x}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/M/J/2025, Q5.





2025 October/November · 9231/11 & 9231/13 · Question 2 · 11 marks
Let
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac32\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\frac32&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Describe the transformation represented by \(A\). [2]
(b) Describe the transformation represented by \(B\). [2]
Triangle \(DEF\) is transformed by \(AB\) onto triangle \(PQR\).
(c) Show that the two triangles have the same area. [2]
(d) Find the invariant lines through the origin of the transformation represented by \(AB\). [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) \(A\) is a shear with the \(x\)-axis fixed and \((0,1)\) mapped to \((3/2,1)\).
(b) \(B\) is a shear with the \(y\)-axis fixed and \((1,0)\) mapped to \((1,3/2)\).
(c) Multiplication gives
\[
AB=\begin{pmatrix}13/4&3/2\\3/2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det(AB)=1,
\]
Therefore the area scale factor is \(|\det(AB)|=1\), so the two triangles have the same area.
(d) For \(y=mx\),
\[
\binom XY
=\begin{pmatrix}13/4&3/2\\3/2&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{x}{mx}
=\binom{(13/4+3m/2)x}{(3/2+m)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
\frac32+m=m\left(\frac{13}{4}+\frac32m\right).
\]
After simplification,
\[
m^2+\frac32m-1=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(m+2)\left(m-\frac12\right)=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{y=-2x\quad\text{or}\quad y=\frac12x}.
\]

 Completed

Sources: Cambridge International 9231/11/O/N/2025, Q2; 9231/13/O/N/2025, Q2.





2025 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks
Let \(k,m\) be non-zero constants and
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&m\end{pmatrix},\quad
C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&1\\1&1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(a) Describe the transformation represented by \(B\) when (i) \(m=1\), and (ii) \(m=k\). [4]
(b) Show that \(ABC\) is singular. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)(i) When \(m=1\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \(B\) represents a one-way stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(k\).
(a)(ii) When \(m=k\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&k\end{pmatrix}=kI,
\]
so \(B\) represents an enlargement with centre the origin and scale factor \(k\).
(b) First,
\[
AB
=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}k&0\\0&m\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}0&m\\-k&m\\k&m\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore
\[
ABC=\begin{pmatrix}
m&m&2m\\
-2k+m&k+m&-k+2m\\
2k+m&-k+m&k+2m
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Expanding its determinant and collecting terms gives
\[
m(k+m)(k+2m)-m(-k+m)(-k+2m)-m(-2k+m)(k+2m)
\]
\[
{}+m(2k+m)(-k+2m)+2m(-2k+m)(-k+m)-2m(2k+m)(k+m)=0.
\]
The six expanded terms simplify to
\[
6m^2k+6m^2k-12m^2k=0.
\]
Hence \(\det(ABC)=0\), so \(ABC\) is singular.

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/12/O/N/2025, Q4.





2025 October/November · 9231/14 · Question 5 · 14 marks
(a) Show that
\[
\cos\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},\qquad
\sin\frac\pi{12}=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
[2]
Let
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&-\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}.
\]
(b) Give full details of the two transformations represented by \(M\), in the correct order. [4]
(c) Write \(M^{-1}\) as the product of two matrices, neither equal to \(I\). [2]
(d) Given that \(y=mx\) is invariant, show that
\[
m^2\sin\frac\pi{12}+2m\cos\frac\pi{12}-\sin\frac\pi{12}=0,
\]
and find \(m\) in the requested cotangent/cosecant form. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(\pi/12=\pi/4-\pi/6\),
\[
\cos\frac\pi{12}
=\cos\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
+\sin\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4},
\]
and
\[
\sin\frac\pi{12}
=\sin\frac\pi4\cos\frac\pi6
-\cos\frac\pi4\sin\frac\pi6
=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}.
\]
(b) The matrix factorises as
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&-\sin(\pi/12)\\\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Reading from right to left, first reflect in the \(x\)-axis, then rotate anticlockwise through \(\pi/12\) about the origin.
(c) Reversing the order and inverting each factor gives
\[
\boxed{M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\pi/12)&\sin(\pi/12)\\-\sin(\pi/12)&\cos(\pi/12)\end{pmatrix}}.
\]
(d) Write \(s=\sin(\pi/12)\) and \(c=\cos(\pi/12)\). A point \((x,mx)\) maps to
\[
\binom XY=\binom{(c+ms)x}{(s-mc)x}.
\]
The condition \(Y=mX\) gives
\[
s-mc=m(c+ms),
\]
so
\[
m^2s+2mc-s=0,
\]
as required. By the quadratic formula,
\[
m=\frac{-2c\pm\sqrt{4c^2+4s^2}}{2s}
=\frac{-c\pm1}{s}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{m=-\cot\frac\pi{12}\pm\cosec\frac\pi{12}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231/14/O/N/2025, Q5.

title: 1.2 Rational functions and graphs
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Rational functions
有理函数写成
\[
y=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)},
\]
其中 \(f(x)\) 与 \(g(x)\) 是多项式，且 \(g(x)\ne0\)。本章只讨论分子与分母次数不超过 2 的情形。


1.2 Intercepts and asymptotes
作图时依次确定以下信息。

与坐标轴的交点：令 \(x=0\) 求 \(y\) 轴交点；令分子等于零求 \(x\) 轴交点。
竖直渐近线：函数在 \(g(x)=0\) 处无定义时，检查该点两侧的符号与趋向。
水平渐近线：比较 \(x\to\pm\infty\) 时分子与分母的最高次项。
斜渐近线：当分子的次数比分母高 1 时，作多项式除法，将函数写成

\[
y=ax+b+\frac{r}{g(x)}.
\]
当 \(x\to\pm\infty\) 时，余项趋于零，所以斜渐近线为 \(y=ax+b\)。


1.3 A five-step sketching method
教材使用以下五步作图法：

求图像与坐标轴的交点；
求竖直渐近线，并判断曲线在渐近线两侧趋向 \(+\infty\) 还是 \(-\infty\)；
求水平或斜渐近线，并判断曲线从哪一侧接近；
求驻点；
综合所有信息完成草图。



1.4 Range by the discriminant method
把有理函数方程重新整理为关于 \(x\) 的二次方程。对于给定的 \(y\)，图像上存在实点的条件是
\[
\Delta\ge0.
\]
因此，令 \(\Delta<0\) 可以找出函数不能取得的 \(y\) 值；再结合渐近线是否能够取到端点，即可写出值域。


1.5 Symmetry

若 \(f(x)=f(-x)\)，则 \(f\) 是偶函数，图像关于 \(y\) 轴对称。
若 \(f(x)=-f(-x)\)，则 \(f\) 是奇函数，图像关于原点具有二阶旋转对称性。



1.6 The curve \(y=|f(x)|\)
先画 \(y=f(x)\)，再把其中位于 \(x\) 轴下方的部分关于 \(x\) 轴反射。原图上的根保持不变，但通常在根处形成尖点。


1.7 The curve \(y=f(|x|)\)
保留 \(y=f(x)\) 在 \(x\ge0\) 的部分，再把这一部分关于 \(y\) 轴反射。所得图像一定关于 \(y\) 轴对称。


1.8 The reciprocal curve \(y=1/f(x)\)
由 \(y=f(x)\) 作 \(y=1/f(x)\) 时：

两图在 \(y=1\) 与 \(y=-1\) 处相交；
两图在同一 \(x\) 处符号相同；
\(f(x)=0\) 的根通常变成 \(1/f(x)\) 的竖直渐近线；
\(f(x)\) 的竖直渐近线变成 \(1/f(x)\) 在 \(x\) 轴上的间断点；
若 \(f(x)\to L\ne0\)，则 \(1/f(x)\to1/L\)；
\(f\) 增加时 \(1/f\) 减少，\(f\) 减少时 \(1/f\) 增加。



1.9 The curve \(y^2=f(x)\)
方程等价于
\[
y=\pm\sqrt{f(x)}.
\]
因此：

图像关于 \(x\) 轴对称；
当 \(f(x)<0\) 时没有实点；
与 \(y=f(x)\) 在 \(y=0\) 和 \(y=1\) 处相交；
若 \(f(x)\) 的根不是驻点，\(y^2=f(x)\) 通常竖直穿过 \(x\) 轴；
对应驻点的 \(x\) 坐标不变，而 \(y\) 坐标变为 \(\pm\sqrt{f(x)}\)。

text:
2. Textbook examples and examination questions

Textbook Examples


Example 4.1 · Pages 96–97
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^2+1}{x^2+2}.
\]
(i) Sketch the graph of \(y=f(x)\).
(ii) State the range of \(f(x)\).
(iii) The equation \(f(x)=k\) has no real solutions. Find the values of \(k\).


Show solution

There are no real zeros of either \(x^2+1\) or \(x^2+2\). Hence the curve has no \(x\)-intercepts and no vertical asymptotes. It passes through
\[
\left(0,\frac12\right).
\]
As \(x\to\pm\infty\),
\[
\frac{x^2+1}{x^2+2}\to1,
\]
so \(y=1\) is a horizontal asymptote, approached from below. Also
\[
f'(x)=\frac{2x}{(x^2+2)^2},
\]
so the only stationary point is the minimum \(\left(0,\frac12\right)\). The graph is symmetrical about the \(y\)-axis.
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\frac12\le f(x)<1}.
\]
The equation \(f(x)=k\) has no real solutions when
\[
\boxed{k<\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad k\ge1}.
\]

Example 4.2 · Pages 103–104
The graph of \(y=f(x)\) has stationary points
\[
P(-1,-10),\qquad Q(3,5).
\]
Sketch:

\(y=|f(x)|\);
\(y=f(|x|)\).




Example 4.2: given curve y = f(x)

The given curve, redrawn from its stated stationary points.   Example 4.2: given curve y = f(x) -5-4-3-2-112345-12-11-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-112345678xyP(−1, −10)Q(3, 5)

For \(y=f(|x|)\), retain only the original curve for \(x\ge0\) and reflect this part in the \(y\)-axis. Thus \(Q(3,5)\) is accompanied by the reflected stationary point \((-3,5)\); the original left-hand part, including \(P\), is not used.

Example 4.3 · Pages 105–106
Given
\[
f(x)=\cos x,
\qquad
g(x)=\tan x,
\]
sketch
\[
y=\frac1{f(x)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
y=\frac1{g(x)}
\]
for \(-360^\circ\le x\le360^\circ\), where \(g(x)\) is undefined at \(x=\pm90^\circ,\pm270^\circ\).


Show solution

The first curve is
\[
y=\sec x.
\]
It has vertical asymptotes where \(\cos x=0\), namely
\[
x=\pm90^\circ,\ \pm270^\circ,
\]
and vertices at the points where \(\cos x=\pm1\).
The second curve is
\[
y=\cot x.
\]
It has vertical asymptotes where \(\tan x=0\), at \(x=-360^\circ,-180^\circ,0,180^\circ,360^\circ\). It has zeros at \(x=\pm90^\circ,\pm270^\circ\), shown as open points here because the stated function \(g\) is itself undefined at those values.

Exercise 4B, Question 4
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[
y=\frac{2x^2+x-1}{x-1}.
\]
Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C\). Show that there is no point on \(C\) for which \(1<y<9\).


Show solution

Since
\[
\frac{2x^2+x-1}{x-1}=2x+3+\frac2{x-1},
\]
the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=1},\qquad\boxed{y=2x+3}.
\]
Rearranging as a quadratic in \(x\) gives
\[
2x^2+(1-y)x+(y-1)=0.
\]
Real \(x\) requires
\[
(1-y)^2-8(y-1)\ge0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(y-1)(y-9)\ge0.
\]
Thus \(y\le1\) or \(y\ge9\), so no point has \(1<y<9\).

 Completed

Exercise 4B, Question 5
The curve \(C\) has equation
\[

\]

\[

Also

\]
For \(p=-1\),
\[

\]
The asymptotes are \(x=2\) and \(y=x+1\). The curve has no \(x\)-intercepts because \(x^2-x+1=0\) has negative discriminant, and its \(y\)-intercept is \(\left(0,-\frac12\right)\).

The curves \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) have equations
\[
C_1:\ y=\frac{ax}{x+5},
\qquad
C_2:\ y=\frac{x^2+(a+10)x+5a+26}{x+5},
\]
respectively, where \(a>2\).
(i) Find the equations of the asymptotes of \(C_1\). [2]
(ii) Find the equation of the oblique asymptote of \(C_2\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) do not intersect. [2]
(iv) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \(C_2\). [3]
(v) Sketch \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) on a single diagram. You do not need to calculate the coordinates of any points where \(C_2\) crosses the axes. [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

For \(C_1\), the asymptotes are
\[
\boxed{x=-5},\qquad\boxed{y=a}.
\]
For \(C_2\),
\[
x^2+(a+10)x+5a+26=(x+5)(x+a+5)+1,
\]
so its oblique asymptote is
\[
\boxed{y=x+a+5}.
\]
Equating the two functions gives
\[
x^2+10x+5a+26=0.
\]
Its discriminant is
\[
100-4(5a+26)=-4-20a<0,
\]
so the curves do not intersect.
Differentiating \(C_2\) gives the stationary-point equation
\[
x^2+10x+24=0,
\]
hence the stationary points are
\[
\boxed{(-4,a+2),\quad(-6,a-2)}.
\]
The sketch must show the common vertical asymptote \(x=-5\), the stated horizontal/oblique asymptotes, the two stationary points of \(C_2\), and no intersection between the curves.

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Quadratic equations
若 \(az^2+bz+c=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta\)，则
\[
\alpha+\beta=-\frac ba,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=\frac ca.
\]
二次方程中所有关于 \(\alpha,\beta\) 的对称函数，都可以用 \(\alpha+\beta\) 与 \(\alpha\beta\) 表示。例如
\[
\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta.
\]


1.2 Cubic equations
若 \(az^3+bz^2+cz+d=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\)，则
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum\alpha
&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\frac ba,\\
\sum\alpha\beta
&=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=\frac ca,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma
&=\alpha\beta\gamma=-\frac da.
\end{aligned}
\]
教材采用以下简写：
\[
\sum\alpha=\alpha+\beta+\gamma,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha.
\]
计算较高次幂和时，可以先求基本对称函数，也可以利用每个根都满足原方程。


1.3 Forming new equations
教材使用两种方法建立新方程：

计算新根的和、两两乘积之和及乘积，再由根与系数关系写出方程；
令新变量与旧变量满足题目给出的根的变换，写出旧变量并代入原方程。

例如新根为 \(2\alpha+1,2\beta+1,2\gamma+1\) 时，令
\[
w=2z+1,
\qquad
z=\frac{w-1}{2}.
\]
新根为 \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\) 时，可以令 \(w=z^2\)，再消去 \(z\)。


1.4 Quartic equations
若 \(az^4+bz^3+cz^2+dz+e=0\) 的根为 \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\)，则
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum\alpha
&=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-\frac ba,\\
\sum\alpha\beta
&=\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta
+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta=\frac ca,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma
&=\alpha\beta\gamma+\beta\gamma\delta
+\gamma\delta\alpha+\delta\alpha\beta=-\frac da,\\
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma\delta
&=\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=\frac ea.
\end{aligned}
\]






提示Sign pattern



从最高次项开始，根的基本对称函数对应的符号依次为
\[
-,\quad +,\quad -,\quad +.
\]

title: 1.1 Roots of polynomial equations
text:
2. Textbook examples and examination questions

Textbook Examples


Example 3.1 · Page 72
Find a quadratic equation with roots \(5\) and \(-3\).


Show solution

The sum of the roots is
\[
5+(-3)=2,
\]
and the product of the roots is
\[
5(-3)=-15.
\]
Taking the coefficient of \(z^2\) to be \(1\), a quadratic equation with the required roots is
\[
\boxed{z^2-2z-15=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.2 · Page 73
The roots of the equation
\[
2z^2+3z+5=0
\]
are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

Find the values of \(\alpha+\beta\) and \(\alpha\beta\).
Find the quadratic equation with roots \(2\alpha\) and \(2\beta\).



Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta=-\frac32,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=\frac52.
\]
For the new roots,
\[
2\alpha+2\beta=2(\alpha+\beta)=-3,
\]
and
\[
(2\alpha)(2\beta)=4\alpha\beta=10.
\]
Therefore the required equation is
\[
\boxed{z^2+3z+10=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.3 · Pages 73–74
The roots of the equation
\[
3z^2-4z-1=0
\]
are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Find the quadratic equation with roots \(\alpha+1\) and \(\beta+1\).


Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta=\frac43,
\qquad
\alpha\beta=-\frac13.
\]
The sum of the new roots is
\[
(\alpha+1)+(\beta+1)=\alpha+\beta+2=\frac{10}{3},
\]
and their product is
\[
(\alpha+1)(\beta+1)
=\alpha\beta+(\alpha+\beta)+1
=2.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{3z^2-10z+6=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.4 · Pages 74–75
The quadratic equation
\[
ax^2+bx+c=0,
\]
where \(a,b,c\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). Prove that
\[
\alpha^2+\beta^2=\frac{b^2-2ac}{a^2}.
\]


Show solution

Since
\[
(\alpha+\beta)^2=\alpha^2+2\alpha\beta+\beta^2,
\]
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2
&=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta\\
&=\left(-\frac ba\right)^2-2\left(\frac ca\right)\\
&=\boxed{\frac{b^2-2ac}{a^2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Example 3.5 · Page 78
The roots of the equation
\[
2z^3-9z^2-27z+54=0
\]
form a geometric progression, so they may be written as \(\dfrac ar,a,ar\). Solve the equation.


Show solution

Using the product of the roots,
\[
\frac ar\times a\times ar=-\frac{54}{2},
\]
so
\[
a^3=-27
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
a=-3.
\]
Using the sum of the roots,
\[
-\frac3r-3-3r=\frac92.
\]
Hence
\[
2r^2+5r+2=0,
\]
so
\[
(2r+1)(r+2)=0
\]
and therefore \(r=-2\) or \(r=-\dfrac12\). Either value gives the same three roots:
\[
\boxed{\frac32,-3,6}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.6 · Pages 78–79
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
x^3-4x^2+x+6=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the values of

\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\);
\(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\).



Show solution

From the original equation,
\[
\sum\alpha=4,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=4^2-2(1)\\
&=\boxed{14}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since each root satisfies \(x^3-4x^2+x+6=0\),
\[
\alpha^3=4\alpha^2-\alpha-6,
\]
with corresponding equations for \(\beta\) and \(\gamma\). Adding them gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3
&=4(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)
-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)-18\\
&=4(14)-4-18\\
&=\boxed{34}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Example 3.7 · Pages 79–80
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
2z^3+5z^2-3z-2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the cubic equation with roots \(2\alpha+1,2\beta+1,2\gamma+1\).


Show solution 1: relations between roots and coefficients

For the original equation,
\[
\sum\alpha=-\frac52,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=-\frac32,
\qquad
\alpha\beta\gamma=1.
\]
For the new roots, their sum is
\[
2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3=-2.
\]
The sum of their products in pairs is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2\alpha+1)(2\beta+1)
+(2\beta+1)(2\gamma+1)
+(2\gamma+1)(2\alpha+1)\\
&=4(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)
+4(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3\\
&=4\left(-\frac32\right)+4\left(-\frac52\right)+3\\
&=-13.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(2\alpha+1)(2\beta+1)(2\gamma+1)\\
&=8\alpha\beta\gamma
+4(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)
+2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+1\\
&=8+4\left(-\frac32\right)
+2\left(-\frac52\right)+1\\
&=-2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the required equation is
\[
\boxed{z^3+2z^2-13z+2=0}.
\]



Show solution 2: substitution method

Let
\[
w=2z+1,
\qquad
z=\frac{w-1}{2}.
\]
Substituting into the original equation gives
\[
2\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)^3
+5\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)^2
-3\left(\frac{w-1}{2}\right)-2=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(4\) and simplifying,
\[
(w-1)^3+5(w-1)^2-6(w-1)-8=0,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{w^3+2w^2-13w+2=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.8 · Pages 80–81
The roots of the cubic equation
\[
2z^3-5z^2+z+2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find the cubic equation with roots \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\).


Show solution

Let \(w=z^2\), so \(z=\sqrt w\). Substitution gives
\[
2w\sqrt w-5w+\sqrt w+2=0.
\]
Collecting the terms containing \(\sqrt w\),
\[
\sqrt w(2w+1)=5w-2.
\]
Squaring both sides,
\[
w(2w+1)^2=(5w-2)^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
4w^3+4w^2+w&=25w^2-20w+4,\\
4w^3-21w^2+21w-4&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the required equation is
\[
\boxed{4w^3-21w^2+21w-4=0}.
\]

 Completed


Example 3.9 · Pages 84–85
The roots of the quartic equation
\[
4z^4+pz^3+qz^2-z+3=0
\]
are \(\alpha,-\alpha,\alpha+\lambda,\alpha-\lambda\), where \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\) are real numbers.

Express \(p\) and \(q\) in terms of \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\).
Show that \(\alpha=-\dfrac12\), and find the values of \(p\) and \(q\).
Give the roots of the quartic equation.



Show solution

The sum of the roots is
\[
\alpha-\alpha+(\alpha+\lambda)+(\alpha-\lambda)
=2\alpha=-\frac p4,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{p=-8\alpha}.
\]
The sum of the products of the roots in pairs simplifies to \(-\lambda^2\). Hence
\[
-\lambda^2=\frac q4
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{q=-4\lambda^2}.
\]
The sum of the products of the roots in threes is
\[
-2\alpha^3.
\]
Since this is equal to \(-\dfrac{-1}{4}=\dfrac14\),
\[
-2\alpha^3=\frac14.
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha^3=-\frac18
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\boxed{\alpha=-\frac12},
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{p=4}.
\]
Using the product of the four roots,
\[
-\alpha^2(\alpha^2-\lambda^2)=\frac34.
\]
Substituting \(\alpha=-\dfrac12\) gives
\[
-\frac14\left(\frac14-\lambda^2\right)=\frac34,
\]
so
\[
\lambda^2=\frac{13}{4}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\boxed{q=-13}.
\]
The roots are
\[
\boxed{
\frac12,
-\frac12,
-\frac12+\frac{\sqrt{13}}2,
-\frac12-\frac{\sqrt{13}}2
}.
\]

 Completed


Examination questions printed in the textbook exercises


Exercise 3B, Question 16
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q5 October/November 2015
The cubic equation
\[
x^3+px^2+qx+r=0,
\]
where \(p,q,r\) are integers, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) such that
\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=15,
\qquad
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=83.
\]
Write down the value of \(p\) and find the value of \(q\).
Given that \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) are all real and that \(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma=36\), find \(\alpha\) and hence find the value of \(r\).


Show solution

Since \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-p\),
\[
\boxed{p=-15}.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
83
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=15^2-2q,
\end{aligned}
\]
so
\[
\boxed{q=71}.
\]
Now
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma
=\alpha(\beta+\gamma)
=\alpha(15-\alpha)=36.
\]
Thus
\[
\alpha^2-15\alpha+36=0,
\]
giving \(\alpha=3\) or \(\alpha=12\).
If \(\alpha=12\), then \(\beta+\gamma=3\) and \(\beta\gamma=35\), which does not give real values of \(\beta,\gamma\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\alpha=3}.
\]
Then \(\beta+\gamma=12\) and \(\beta\gamma=35\), so
\[
r=-\alpha\beta\gamma=-3(35)=\boxed{-105}.
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3B, Question 17
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q2 October/November 2013
The cubic equation
\[
x^3-px-q=0,
\]
where \(p,q\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Show that

\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=2p\);
\(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=3q\);
\[
6(\alpha^5+\beta^5+\gamma^5)
=5(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)
(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2).
\]



Show solution

For the original equation,
\[
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0,
\qquad
\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-p.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2
-2(\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha)\\
&=0-2(-p)\\
&=\boxed{2p}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each root satisfies \(x^3=px+q\). Adding the three corresponding equations gives
\[
\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3
=p(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)+3q
=\boxed{3q}.
\]
Multiplying \(x^3=px+q\) by \(x^2\) gives \(x^5=px^3+qx^2\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^5+\beta^5+\gamma^5
&=p(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3)
+q(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)\\
&=p(3q)+q(2p)\\
&=5pq.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus both sides of the required identity are equal to \(30pq\).

 Completed


Exercise 3B, Question 18
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q1 October/November 2011
The equation
\[
x^3+px+q=0
\]
has a repeated root. Prove that
\[
4p^3+27q^2=0.
\]


Show solution

Let the repeated root be \(\alpha\) and the third root be \(\beta\). Since the coefficient of \(x^2\) is zero,
\[
2\alpha+\beta=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\beta=-2\alpha.
\]
Using the sum of the products in pairs,
\[
p=\alpha^2+2\alpha\beta
=\alpha^2-4\alpha^2
=-3\alpha^2.
\]
Using the product of the roots,
\[
-q=\alpha^2\beta=-2\alpha^3,
\]
so \(q=2\alpha^3\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
4p^3+27q^2
&=4(-3\alpha^2)^3+27(2\alpha^3)^2\\
&=-108\alpha^6+108\alpha^6\\
&=\boxed{0}.
\end{aligned}
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3C, Question 7
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q11 October/November 2014
The roots of the quartic equation
\[
x^4+4x^3+2x^2-4x+1=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\). Find the values of

\(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta\);
\(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2\);
\(\dfrac1\alpha+\dfrac1\beta+\dfrac1\gamma+\dfrac1\delta\);
\[
\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\beta}{\alpha\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta\delta}
+\frac{\delta}{\alpha\beta\gamma}.
\]

Using the substitution \(y=x+1\), find a quartic equation in \(y\). Solve this quartic equation and hence find the roots of
\[
x^4+4x^3+2x^2-4x+1=0.
\]


Show solution

From the coefficients,
\[
\sum\alpha=-4,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=2,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta\gamma=4,
\qquad
\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-4},
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2
&=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)^2-2\sum\alpha\beta\\
&=16-4\\
&=\boxed{12},
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma+\frac1\delta
=\frac{\sum\alpha\beta\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}
=\boxed{4}.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\beta}{\alpha\gamma\delta}
+\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta\delta}
+\frac{\delta}{\alpha\beta\gamma}\\
&=\frac{\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2+\delta^2}
{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}\\
&=\boxed{12}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(y=x+1\), so \(x=y-1\). Substitution gives
\[
y^4-4y^2+4=0,
\]
or
\[
(y^2-2)^2=0.
\]
Thus \(y=\pm\sqrt2\), each repeated, and the roots of the original equation are
\[
\boxed{-1+\sqrt2,\ -1+\sqrt2,\ -1-\sqrt2,\ -1-\sqrt2}.
\]

 Completed


Exercise 3C, Question 8
Source: 9231 Paper 11 Q11 October/November 2012
The roots of the equation
\[
x^4-3x^2+5x-2=0
\]
are \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\), and
\[
S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n+\delta^n.
\]
Show that
\[
S_{n+4}-3S_{n+2}+5S_{n+1}-2S_n=0.
\]
Find the values of

\(S_2\) and \(S_4\);
\(S_3\) and \(S_5\).

Hence find the value of
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\alpha^2(\beta^3+\gamma^3+\delta^3)
+\beta^2(\gamma^3+\delta^3+\alpha^3)\\
&\quad+\gamma^2(\delta^3+\alpha^3+\beta^3)
+\delta^2(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3).
\end{aligned}
\]


Show solution

Each root satisfies
\[
x^4-3x^2+5x-2=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(x^n\) and then adding the four resulting equations gives
\[
\boxed{S_{n+4}-3S_{n+2}+5S_{n+1}-2S_n=0}.
\]
From the coefficients,
\[
S_1=0,
\qquad
\sum\alpha\beta=-3,
\]
so
\[
S_2=S_1^2-2\sum\alpha\beta=\boxed{6}.
\]
Taking \(n=0\) in the recurrence, with \(S_0=4\), gives
\[
S_4-3S_2+5S_1-2S_0=0,
\]
and hence
\[
S_4=\boxed{26}.
\]
Also, \(\sum\alpha\beta\gamma=-5\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_3
&=\left(\sum\alpha\right)^3
-3\left(\sum\alpha\right)\left(\sum\alpha\beta\right)
+3\sum\alpha\beta\gamma\\
&=0-0+3(-5)\\
&=\boxed{-15}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(n=1\) in the recurrence gives
\[
S_5-3S_3+5S_2-2S_1=0,
\]
so
\[
S_5=\boxed{-75}.
\]
The final expression is
\[
S_2S_3-S_5
=6(-15)-(-75)
=\boxed{-15}.
\]

 Completed

Power sumsTransformed roots★★★☆☆
The equation
\[x^3-x+1=0\]
has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(i) Use the relation \(x=y^{1/3}\) to show that the equation
\[y^3+3y^2+2y+1=0\]
has roots \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\). Hence write down the value of \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\). [3]
Let \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n\).
(ii) Find the value of \(S_{-3}\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(S_6=5\) and find the value of \(S_9\). [4]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Put \(y=x^3\), so \(x=y^{1/3}\). Then
\[
y-y^{1/3}+1=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
y+1=y^{1/3}.
\]
Cubing both sides,
\[y=(y+1)^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^3+3y^2+2y+1=0. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
The three roots are \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\), so Vieta’s formula gives \(\boxed{S_3=-3}\). B1
(ii) For the roots \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\), the sum of pairwise products is \(2\) and the product is \(-1\). Hence
\[S_{-3}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(iii)
\[S_6=S_3^2-2(2)=(-3)^2-4=5. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
Summing the transformed equation over its three roots gives
\[S_9+3S_6+2S_3+3=0,\]
so
\[S_9=-3(5)-2(-3)-3=-12. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

2019 May/June · 9231/13 · Question 9 · 11 marks
Unknown coefficientsSymmetric sums★★★★☆
A cubic equation
\[x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\]
has real roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) such that
\[
\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma=-\frac5{12},
\qquad \alpha\beta\gamma=-12,
\qquad \alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=90.
\]
(i) Find the values of \(c\) and \(d\). [3]
(ii) Express \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\) in terms of \(b\). [2]
(iii) Show that \(b^3-15b+126=0\). [4]
(iv) Given that \(3+i\sqrt{12}\) is a root of \(y^3-15y+126=0\), deduce the value of \(b\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(i) Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-d=-12\), \(d=12\). B1
Also
\[\frac{\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=-\frac5{12},\]
so \(c=\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=5\). M1 A1
(ii)
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)^2-2c=b^2-10. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(iii) Since \(S_2=b^2-10\) and every root satisfies \(x^3=-bx^2-5x-12\), summing over all three roots gives
\[90=-b(b^2-10)-5(-b)-36.\]
Hence
\[b^3-15b+126=0. \qquad \text{M1 M1 A1 A1}\]
(iv) The polynomial has real coefficients, so \(3-i\sqrt{12}\) is also a root. These two roots have sum \(6\). Since the coefficient of \(y^2\) is zero, the third root is \(-6\). Thus the required real value is \(\boxed{b=-6}\). M1 A1

Transformed rootsPower sums★★★★☆
The equation \(x^3+2x^2+x+7=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(i) Use the relation \(x^2=-7y\) to show that
\[49y^3+14y^2-27y+7=0\]
has roots
\[\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma},\qquad
\frac{\beta}{\gamma\alpha},\qquad
\frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta}. \qquad \textbf{[4]}\]
(ii) Show that
\[\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta^2\gamma^2}+
\frac{\beta^2}{\gamma^2\alpha^2}+
\frac{\gamma^2}{\alpha^2\beta^2}=\frac{58}{49}. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
(iii) Find the exact value of
\[
\frac{\alpha^3}{\beta^3\gamma^3}+
\frac{\beta^3}{\gamma^3\alpha^3}+
\frac{\gamma^3}{\alpha^3\beta^3}. \qquad \textbf{[2]}
\]


Show answer and mark scheme

Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-7\),
\[\frac{\alpha}{\beta\gamma}=-\frac{\alpha^2}{7},\]
and similarly for the other two roots. With \(x^2=-7y\), the original equation becomes
\[
x(1-7y)+7(1-2y)=0,
\]
so \(x=7(2y-1)/(1-7y)\). Squaring and using \(x^2=-7y\) gives
\[
49(2y-1)^2=-7y(1-7y)^2,
\]
which simplifies to the stated cubic. M1 M1 A1 A1
For the transformed roots,
\[e_1=-\frac27,\qquad e_2=-\frac{27}{49},\qquad e_3=-\frac17.\]
Therefore
\[p_2=e_1^2-2e_2=\frac4{49}+\frac{54}{49}=\frac{58}{49}. \qquad \text{M1 A1 A1}\]
Also
\[p_3=e_1p_2-e_2p_1+3e_3=-\frac{317}{343}. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

Squared rootsUnknown coefficient★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(6x^3+px^2-3x-5=0\), where \(p\) is a constant, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^2,\beta^2,\gamma^2\). [3]
(b) It is given that
\[\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma).\]
(i) Find the value of \(p\). [3]
(ii) Find the value of \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=x^2\). Rewriting the original equation gives \(x(6y-3)=5-py\). Squaring and using \(x^2=y\) gives
\[y(6y-3)^2=(5-py)^2,\]
hence
\[36y^3-(p^2+36)y^2+(10p+9)y-25=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b)(i)
\[\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\frac p6,\qquad
\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=-\frac12.\]
Thus
\[\frac{p^2}{36}+1=-\frac p3,\]
so \((p+6)^2=0\) and \(p=-6\). M1 A1 A1
(b)(ii) With \(p=-6\),
\[e_1=1,\qquad e_2=-\frac12,\qquad e_3=\frac56,\]
and
\[\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=e_1^3-3e_1e_2+3e_3=5. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

The cubic equation \(7x^3+3x^2+5x+1=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).

(b) Find \(\alpha^{-2}+\beta^{-2}+\gamma^{-2}\). [2]
(c) Find \(\alpha^{-3}+\beta^{-3}+\gamma^{-3}\). [2]

\[
\frac7{y^3}+\frac3{y^2}+\frac5y+1=0.

(b)

Cubed rootsSingular matrix★★★★☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+cx+1=0\), where \(c\) is a constant, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3\). [3]
(b) Show that \(\alpha^6+\beta^6+\gamma^6=3-2c^3\). [3]
(c) Find the real value of \(c\) for which
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\alpha^3&\beta^3\\
\alpha^3&1&\gamma^3\\
\beta^3&\gamma^3&1
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is singular. [5]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=x^3\). Since \(cx=-(y+1)\), cubing and using \(x^3=y\) gives \(c^3y=-(y+1)^3\), hence
\[y^3+3y^2+(c^3+3)y+1=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b) For the new roots, \(e_1=-3\) and \(e_2=c^3+3\). Hence
\[\alpha^6+\beta^6+\gamma^6=(-3)^2-2(c^3+3)=3-2c^3. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(c) Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-1\),
\[\alpha^3\beta^3\gamma^3=-1.\]
The determinant is
\[1-(\alpha^6+\beta^6+\gamma^6)+2\alpha^3\beta^3\gamma^3=2c^3-4.\]
Therefore \(c^3=2\) and
\[c=\sqrt[3]{2}. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1 M1 A1}\]

2020 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 1 · 8 marks
Linear transformationUnknown coefficients★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\), where \(b,c,d\) are constants, has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). It is given that \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-1\).
(a) State the value of \(d\). [1]
(b) Find a cubic equation, with coefficients in terms of \(b\) and \(c\), whose roots are \(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+1\). [3]
(c) Given also that \(\gamma+1=-\alpha-1\), deduce that
\[(c-2b+3)(b-3)=b-c. \qquad \textbf{[4]}\]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Since \(\alpha\beta\gamma=-d=-1\), \(d=1\). B1
(b) The transformed roots have
\[e_1'=3-b,\qquad e_2'=c-2b+3,\qquad e_3'=c-b.\]
Thus the required equation is
\[x^3+(b-3)x^2+(c-2b+3)x+(b-c)=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(c) Write the transformed roots as \(r,-r,s\). Their sum gives \(s=3-b\). Also their pairwise sum is \(-r^2=e_2'\) and their product is \(-r^2s=e_3'\). Hence
\[e_3'=e_2'(3-b).\]
Therefore
\[c-b=(c-2b+3)(3-b),\]
which is equivalent to the required result. B1 B1 M1 A1

Quartic equationPower sums★★★★☆
The equation \(x^4-2x^3-1=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\).
(a) Find a quartic equation whose roots are \(\alpha^3,\beta^3,\gamma^3,\delta^3\) and state the value of \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3+\delta^3\). [4]
(b) Find
\[\frac1{\alpha^3}+\frac1{\beta^3}+\frac1{\gamma^3}+\frac1{\delta^3}. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
(c) Find \(\alpha^4+\beta^4+\gamma^4+\delta^4\). [2]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=x^3\). Since \(x^4=2x^3+1\) and no root is zero,
\[
x=2+\frac1y=\frac{2y+1}{y}.
\]
Cubing and using \(x^3=y\) gives
\[y^4-(2y+1)^3=0,\]
so
\[y^4-8y^3-12y^2-6y-1=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
Hence \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3+\delta^3=8\). B1
(b) For the transformed equation, \(e_3=6\) and \(e_4=-1\). Therefore
\[\sum\frac1{\alpha^3}=\frac{e_3}{e_4}=-6. \qquad \text{M1 A1 A1}\]
(c) Since \(x^4=2x^3+1\) for every root,
\[\alpha^4+\beta^4+\gamma^4+\delta^4=2(8)+4=20. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

The cubic equation \(2x^3-4x^2+3=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Let
\[S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n+\gamma^n.\]
(a) State the value of \(S_1\) and find the value of \(S_2\). [3]
(b)(i) Express \(S_{n+3}\) in terms of \(S_{n+2}\) and \(S_n\). [1]
(b)(ii) Hence, or otherwise, find \(S_4\). [2]
(c) Use the substitution \(y=S_1-x\), where \(S_1\) is the numerical value found in part (a), to find and simplify an equation whose roots are \(\alpha+\beta,\beta+\gamma,\gamma+\alpha\). [3]
(d) Find
\[\frac1{\alpha+\beta}+\frac1{\beta+\gamma}+\frac1{\gamma+\alpha}. \qquad \textbf{[2]}\]


Show answer and mark scheme

\[S_2=S_1^2-2e_2=4. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b)(i) From \(2x^3-4x^2+3=0\),
\[S_{n+3}=2S_{n+2}-\frac32S_n. \qquad \text{B1}\]
(b)(ii) Taking \(n=0\) in the recurrence gives
\[
S_3=2S_2-\frac32S_0=2(4)-\frac32(3)=\frac72.
\]
Taking \(n=1\) then gives
\[S_4=2S_3-\frac32S_1=4. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(c) Put \(x=2-y\):
\[2(2-y)^3-4(2-y)^2+3=0,\]
which simplifies to
\[2y^3-8y^2+8y-3=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]

It is given that

\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=6.

The cubic equation \(x^3+bx^2+cx+d=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Find \(b,c,d\). [6]

2021 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks
Power sumsSummation★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+2x^2+3x+3=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\). [2]
(b) Show that \(\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=1\). [2]
(c) Use standard results from the list of formulae (MF19) to show that
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left((\alpha+r)^3+(\beta+r)^3+(\gamma+r)^3\right)
=n+\frac14n(n+1)(an^2+bn+c),
\]
where \(a,b,c\) are constants to be determined. [6]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a)
\[p_2=(-2)^2-2(3)=-2. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]
(b) Summing the original equation over the roots,
\[p_3+2p_2+3p_1+9=0,\]
so \(p_3=1\). M1 A1
(c) For each \(r\),
\[
(\alpha+r)^3+(\beta+r)^3+(\gamma+r)^3
=p_3+3rp_2+3r^2p_1+3r^3.
\]
Using \(p_1=-2\), \(p_2=-2\) and \(p_3=1\), expand
\[\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(1-6r-6r^2+3r^3\right). \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
Using the standard sums and simplifying gives
\[n+\frac14n(n+1)(3n^2-5n-16). \qquad \text{M1 M1 A1}\]
Thus
\[a=3,\qquad b=-5,\qquad c=-16.\]

Reciprocal powersTransformed roots★★★★☆
The cubic equation \(2x^3+5x^2-6=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find a cubic equation whose roots are \(1/\alpha^3,1/\beta^3,1/\gamma^3\). [3]
(b) Find
\[\frac1{\alpha^6}+\frac1{\beta^6}+\frac1{\gamma^6}. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
(c) Find also
\[\frac1{\alpha^9}+\frac1{\beta^9}+\frac1{\gamma^9}. \qquad \textbf{[2]}\]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) First put \(t=1/x\). Dividing the original equation by \(x^3\) gives
\[
2+5t-6t^3=0,
\]
so the reciprocal roots satisfy \(6t^3-5t-2=0\). Now put \(y=t^3\). Then
\[
5t=6y-2.
\]
Cubing and using \(t^3=y\) gives
\[
125y=(6y-2)^3.
\]
Expanding and simplifying gives
\[216y^3-216y^2-53y-8=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(b) For the transformed roots,
\[e_1=1,\qquad e_2=-\frac{53}{216}.\]
Therefore
\[p_2=1-2\left(-\frac{53}{216}\right)=\frac{161}{108}. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
(c) If \(z\) is one of the transformed roots, then
\[
216z^3-216z^2-53z-8=0.
\]
Summing this equation over all three transformed roots gives
\[216S_{-9}=216S_{-6}+53S_{-3}+24.\]
Since \(S_{-3}=1\),
\[S_{-9}=\frac{133}{72}. \qquad \text{M1 A1}\]

Symmetric sumsSingular matrix★★★☆☆
The cubic equation \(x^3+5x^2+10x-2=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Find \(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\). [3]
(b) Show that

The quartic equation
\[x^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx-2=0\]
has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\). It is given that

2023 October/November · 9231/12 · Question 4 · 10 marks
Linear transformationPositive and negative powers★★★★☆
The cubic equation \(27x^3+18x^2+6x-1=0\) has roots \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\).
(a) Show that a cubic equation with roots \(3\alpha+1,3\beta+1,3\gamma+1\) is
\[y^3-y^2+y-2=0. \qquad \textbf{[3]}\]
The sum \((3\alpha+1)^n+(3\beta+1)^n+(3\gamma+1)^n\) is denoted by \(S_n\).
(b) Find \(S_2\) and \(S_3\). [4]
(c) Find \(S_{-1}\) and \(S_{-2}\). [3]


Show answer and mark scheme

(a) Put \(y=3x+1\), so \(x=(y-1)/3\). Then
\[
27\left(\frac{y-1}{3}\right)^3
+18\left(\frac{y-1}{3}\right)^2
+6\left(\frac{y-1}{3}\right)-1=0.
\]
Expanding and simplifying gives
\[y^3-y^2+y-2=0. \qquad \text{B1 M1 A1}\]
For the transformed roots, \(e_1=1\), \(e_2=1\), \(e_3=2\).
(b)

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
1. 教材知识点

1.1 Sequences, series and sigma notation
数列是按顺序排列的数；级数是数列各项的和。若通项为 \(u_r\)，前 \(n\) 项和写作
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r.
\]
上下限决定所包含的项。若求和式中没有 \(r\)，仍需按上下限重复相加，例如
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}c=nc.
\]
若已知前 \(n\) 项和，则
\[
u_1=S_1,\qquad u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}\quad(r\ge2).
\]


1.2 Standard results
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1),
\]
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^2=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1),
\]
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r^3=\frac14n^2(n+1)^2.
\]
使用时先展开通项，再利用求和的线性性质。不要把 \(\sum r^2\) 误写成 \(\left(\sum r\right)^2\)。


1.3 Changing limits
对于连续的一段整数，可用“大和减小和”：
\[
\sum_{r=a}^{b}u_r
=\sum_{r=1}^{b}u_r-\sum_{r=1}^{a-1}u_r.
\]
同理，若 \(S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\)，则
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n.
\]


1.4 Method of differences
核心是把通项写成相邻项之差：
\[
u_r=f(r)-f(r+1).
\]
于是
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r
=[f(1)-f(2)]+[f(2)-f(3)]+\cdots+[f(n)-f(n+1)],
\]
中间项全部消去，只剩
\[
\boxed{S_n=f(1)-f(n+1)}.
\]
若裂项跨度大于 1，通常会留下多于一个首项和尾项，必须将前几项与最后几项完整写出。


1.5 Sum to infinity
先求有限前 \(n\) 项和 \(S_n\)，再直接考察
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n.
\]
若极限存在且有限，则级数收敛，且该极限就是无穷和。若 \(u_n\not\to0\)，级数一定不收敛；但 \(u_n\to0\) 本身不能保证收敛。

title: 1.3 Summation of series
text:
2. Textbook Examples

Example 2.1 · Pages 43–44
For the series
\[
2+5+8+\cdots+500,
\]
(i) find a formula for the \(r\)th term \(u_r\); (ii) find the number of terms; (iii) find the sum by reversing and adding; (iv) confirm the answer using sigma notation.


Show solution

The sequence has common difference \(3\), so
\[
u_r=3r-1.
\]
Since \(3r-1=500\), there are \(167\) terms. Reversing and adding gives
\[
2S=167(2+500),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{S=41917}.
\]
Also
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{167}(3r-1)
=3\cdot\frac{167\cdot168}{2}-167
=41917.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.2 · Page 44
Calculate the sum of the integers from \(100\) to \(200\) inclusive.


Show solution

\[
\sum_{r=100}^{200}r
=\sum_{r=1}^{200}r-\sum_{r=1}^{99}r
=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}-\frac{99\cdot100}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{15150}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.3 · Page 47
Given \(u_r=r^2+2r-1\):

write down the first three terms;
find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r\);
check the result for \(n=3\).



Show solution

The first three terms are \(2,7,14\). Also
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r-1)
&=\sum r^2+2\sum r-\sum1\\
&=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+n(n+1)-n\\
&=\boxed{\frac16n(2n^2+9n+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(n=3\), the formula gives \(23\), and \(2+7+14=23\).

 Completed


Example 2.4 · Page 48
Write
\[
(1\times3)+(2\times4)+(3\times5)+\cdots+n(n+2)
\]
using sigma notation, and hence find its sum.


Show solution

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}(r^2+2r).
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+2)=\frac16n(n+1)(2n+7)}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.5 · Page 50
Calculate
\[
5+10+20+40+\cdots+2560+5120.
\]


Show solution

Let the sum be \(S\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=5+10+20+\cdots+2560+5120,\\
2S&=10+20+40+\cdots+5120+10240.
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting gives \(S=10240-5\), hence
\[
\boxed{S=10235}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.6 · Pages 50–51
(i) Show that
\[
\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}=\frac1{r(r+1)}.
\]
(ii) Hence find
\[
\frac1{1\times2}+\frac1{2\times3}+\cdots+\frac1{30\times31}.
\]


Show solution

The identity follows by combining the two fractions. Therefore
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{30}\frac1{r(r+1)}
=\sum_{r=1}^{30}\left(\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}\right)
=1-\frac1{31}.
\]
Hence the sum is
\[
\boxed{\frac{30}{31}}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.7 · Page 52
(i) Show that \((2r+1)^2-(2r-1)^2=8r\).
(ii) Hence find \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r\).
(iii) Deduce the standard result for \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r\).


Show solution

Expanding proves the identity. Summing gives
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r
=(3^2-1^2)+(5^2-3^2)+\cdots+[(2n+1)^2-(2n-1)^2].
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}8r=(2n+1)^2-1=4n^2+4n,
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac12n(n+1)}.
\]

 Completed


Example 2.8 · Pages 52–53
(i) Show that
\[
\frac2r-\frac3{r+1}+\frac1{r+2}
=\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
\]
(ii) Hence find
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}\frac{r+4}{r(r+1)(r+2)}.
\]
(iii) Deduce the sum to infinity.


Show solution

After using the stated decomposition and writing the first and last terms, all middle terms cancel, leaving
\[
S_n=\frac32-\frac2{n+1}+\frac1{n+2}
=\frac{n(3n+7)}{2(n+1)(n+2)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{S_\infty=\frac32}.
\]

 Completed

Exercise 2B, Question 11
It is given that
\[
S_n=\sum_{r=1}^{n}u_r=2n^2+n.
\]
Write down \(S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4\). Express \(u_r\) in terms of \(r\), justifying your answer. Find
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r.
\]


Show solution

\[
S_1=3,\quad S_2=10,\quad S_3=21,\quad S_4=36.
\]
For \(r\ge2\),
\[
u_r=S_r-S_{r-1}=4r-1,
\]
and this also gives \(u_1=3\). Finally,
\[
\sum_{r=n+1}^{2n}u_r=S_{2n}-S_n
=\boxed{6n^2+n}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 3, October/November 2013.



Exercise 2C, Question 11
Given that
\[
u_k=\frac1{2k-1}-\frac1{2k+1},
\]
express \(\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k\) in terms of \(n\) and deduce \(\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k\).


Show solution

\[
\sum_{k=13}^{n}u_k
=\left(\frac1{25}-\frac1{27}\right)+\cdots+
\left(\frac1{2n-1}-\frac1{2n+1}\right)
=\boxed{\frac1{25}-\frac1{2n+1}}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\sum_{k=13}^{\infty}u_k=\frac1{25}}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 1, October/November 2014.



Exercise 2C, Question 12
For positive integers \(n\),
\[
a_n=\frac{n+5}{n^2-n+1}-\frac{n+6}{n^2+n+1},
\]
and \(S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}a_n\). Find \(S_{30}\) correct to 3 decimal places and the least \(N\) for which \(S_N>4.9\).


Show solution

Successive terms telescope because the second fraction in \(a_n\) is the first fraction in \(a_{n+1}\). Thus
\[
S_N=6-\frac{N+6}{N^2+N+1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
S_{30}=6-\frac{36}{931}=\boxed{5.961}\quad\text{(3 d.p.)}.
\]
Checking successive values gives \(S_2<4.9\) and \(S_3>4.9\), so
\[
\boxed{N=3}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2015.



Exercise 2C, Question 13
Let \(f(r)=r(r+1)(r+2)\).

Show that \(f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)\).
Hence show that \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)\).
Using the standard result for \(\sum r\), deduce the standard result for \(\sum r^2\).
Find the sum

\[
1^2+2(2^2)+3^2+2(4^2)+\cdots+2(n-1)^2+n^2,
\]
where \(n\) is odd.


Show solution

Summing \(f(r)-f(r-1)=3r(r+1)\) gives
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{n}r(r+1)=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2).
\]
Since \(r(r+1)=r^2+r\),
\[
\sum r^2=\frac13n(n+1)(n+2)-\frac12n(n+1)
=\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)}.
\]
For the final series, add one extra copy of every even square to the usual sum of squares. With \(m=(n-1)/2\),
\[
\boxed{\frac16n(n+1)(2n+1)+\frac23m(m+1)(2m+1)}.
\]

 Completed

Source: Cambridge International 9231 Paper 11, Question 4, October/November 2012.
